q-18101.name: Question 1
q-18101.problem: Given that $(x+3)$ and $(x-1)$ are factors of $f(x)=a{x}^{3}+7{x}^{2}+bx-9,$ then $a+b=$
q-18101.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x=r$ is also a root of $f(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factors $(x+3)$ and $(x-1).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3=0 & \,⇒\,x=-3 \\ x-1=0 & \,⇒\,x=1\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+3)$ and $(x-1)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=-3$ and $x=1$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f(-3)=0$ and $f(1)=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) & =0 \\ a(-3)^{3}+7(-3)^{2}+b(-3)-9 & =0 \\ -27a-3b+63-9 & =0 \\ -27a-3b & =-54 \\ -9a-b & =-18, \\  \\ f(1) & =0 \\ a(1)^{3}+7(1)^{2}+b(1)-9 & =0 \\ a+b+7-9 & =0 \\ a+b & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-9a-b=-18 \\ a+b=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we eliminate $b$ and get

$$
-8a=-16\,⇒\,a=2.
$$

Substituting $a=2$ in either equation gives $b=0.$ So our solutions are $a=2$ and $b=0.$ Finally then,

$$
a+b=2+0=2.
$$

q-18956.name: Question 2
q-18956.problem: If $(x+5)$ is a factor of $p(x)=3{x}^{2}+14x+c,$ then $c=$
q-18956.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ then the root $x=r$ is also a root of $p(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factor $(x+5).$ The root of this factor can be found by setting the factor equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5 & =0 \\ x & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+5)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ the root $x=-5$ is also a root of $p(x).$ This means $p(-5)=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}p(-5) & =0 \\ 3(-5)^{2}+14(-5)+c & =0 \\ 75-70+c & =0 \\ c & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

q-112536.name: Question 3
q-112536.problem: Given that $(2x-1)$ and $(x+2)$ are factors of $f(x)=a{x}^{3}+b{x}^{2}-2x$, then $a+b=$
q-112536.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x=r$ is also a root of $f(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factors $(2x-1)$ and $(x+2).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-1=0 & \,⇒\,x=\frac{1}{2} \\ x+2=0 & \,⇒\,x=-2\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(2x-1)$ and $(x+2)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and $x=-2$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f(\frac{1}{2})=0$ and $f(-2)=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\frac{1}{2}) & =0 \\ a{(\frac{1}{2})}^{3}+b{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}-2(\frac{1}{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{1}{8}a+\frac{1}{4}b-1 & =0 \\ a+2b-8 & =0 \\ a+2b & =8, \\  \\ f(-2) & =0 \\ a(-2)^{3}+b(-2)^{2}-2(-2) & =0 \\ -8a+4b+4 & =0 \\ -8a+4b & =-4 \\ 2a-b & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}a+2b=8 \\ 2a-b=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Eliminating $b,$ we get

$$
5a=10\,⇒\,a=2.
$$

Substituting $a=2$ in either equation gives $b=3.$ So our solutions are $a=2$ and $b=3.$ Finally then,

$$
a+b=2+3=5.
$$
